waivers.reason: No module ships a roles file yet: the roles file has no FxTS spec to be written against, and the hub still uses its own flat roles.
The OT module is hub-hosted Python with its own layout; no module SDK template exists for a hub-hosted module.
The record id rule of the transport contract (T-5) is not built: records carry an id the adapter makes, and the hub does not yet keep each id once.

The module has a store-and-forward buffer of its own for acquisition, but not the transport contract's (T-6): no declared capacity on the hub link, no replay at a separate rate, and buffering is not on its health.
The goodbye and the last will of the transport contract (T-8) are not built: the hub learns of a shutdown only when calls stop.
Command expiry (T-11) is not built: a process-control write carries no expiry for the module to refuse it by.

metadata.state: Forge's own OT module: PLC and OPC UA connections, the tag engine, alarms and control writes. It carries one identity since 2026-11-18, the approved FACTS spec's, in its manifest file and in the manifest its code registers with (FB-144).
metadata.time_contract_state: Its plant-floor connections are declared in the FACTS spec's time_governance (OPC UA current time, class T0). M-4 to M-7 are run by the conformance kit through the module's own hook (src/forge/modules/ot/conformance.py): the adapter on a real tag registry with two stamped tags, against a reference hub. No PLC or OPC UA server is connected, so a connection's clock gate is not exercised by the kit; its own tests cover it.
metadata.note: The local SQLite store-and-forward buffer is not declared as a database; whether M-8 covers it is the owner's to decide (FB-147).
